subject: BrightStack traffic declaration — preliminary sizing review
content:
From: Elena Morales <elena@brightstack.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightStack Eng Team <eng-team@brightstack.ai>
Date: 2028-11-13T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: BrightStack traffic declaration — preliminary sizing review

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached is our initial traffic declaration CSV (brightstack_traffic_declaration_v1.csv) with the numbers the product team asked us to share for a preliminary sizing. High-level summary below so you don’t have to open the file right away: 

- Daily active users (DAU): ~150,000
- Average requests/day: ~1.9M
- Typical RPS distribution: baseline 120 RPS sustained, peak bursts up to ~1,200 RPS (10m windows)
- Concurrency (approx): expected concurrent sessions during peak ~1,800 (includes streaming connections)
- Prompt length distribution: 60% short (<32 tokens), 35% medium (32–256 tokens), 5% long (>256 tokens)
- Response lengths (tokens): median 32, mean 40, 95th pct 120
- Model targets: primarily an open-chat 33B for assistant flows, fallback to 13B for lower-cost paths
- Caching: we have a heavy prefix reuse pattern for assistant flows — estimate ~70% prefix overlap within a session (system prompts repeated)
- Streaming: yes, ~40% of flows prefer streaming (progressive output)
- Latency SLO: target 95th <= 250 ms for short flows; willing to accept up to 1,200 ms for >256 token responses
- Compliance: data retention strict; all inference request logs must be encrypted at rest and purged per our retention policy (30 days)

We attached a CSV with time-of-day RPS, percentiles, and a small sample prompt set. Please let us know if you need any clarifications — the product team is happy to fill in anything missing. We’re trying to lock down a recommended reserved capacity before our procurement review the week of Nov 27.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Product, BrightStack

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightstack.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-14T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightStack traffic declaration — preliminary sizing review

Elena — thanks for the data and the CSV, that’s exactly the level we need to start a preliminary sizing. A few quick clarifying Qs from our side to make the baseline more accurate before we propose GPU counts: 

1) Model mix: you mentioned a 'primary 33B' and fallback 13B — what percentage of requests do you expect to hit each model at launch (approx)?
2) KV / prefix caching: when you say ~70% prefix overlap, is that within the same user session (i.e., single conversation) or across sessions (shared system prompt across many users)? This affects how much of the KV cache can be reused across requests.
3) Streaming vs non-streaming: of the 40% streaming flows, are those short-response streaming only (e.g., token-by-token for short prompts) or also used for long-response generation?
4) Tokenization & token budgets: do the prompt token counts in the CSV include encoder tokens + system prompt? If you have a few representative sample prompts (you included some), can you flag which are short/med/long?
5) P50 vs P95 concurrency windows: can you attach a 1-hour sample window showing the per-minute concurrent sessions during peak? That helps us size batching and ghosts for GPU utilization.
6) Quantization/precision: are you comfortable with 8-bit dynamic quantization, or do you require FP16/Half for parity reasons?
7) Compliance constraints: do any workloads require data to remain in-region (we have US West and US East options) or air-gapped handling?

If you can reply with short answers we’ll run a quick estimate and send back a recommended dedicated pool (GPU SKU counts + autoscale policy + cost ballpark) by EOD Friday. If it’s easier, we can run a 30–45 minute workshop tomorrow to walk through the sample prompts and traffic windows.

I’m looping Marissa (solutions) and Vivek (pre-sales infra) to prepare the sizing assumptions doc.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

---

From: Elena Morales <elena@brightstack.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightStack Eng Team <eng-team@brightstack.ai>
Date: 2028-11-15T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightStack traffic declaration — preliminary sizing review

Sean — quick answers inline: 

1) Model mix: expect ~70% requests to use the 33B path, ~25% to use 13B, and ~5% to hit a smaller 7B path for ephemeral assistant previews. We’ll more aggressively move to 13B for low-cost customers over time.
2) Caching: the 70% prefix reuse is primarily within-session (same conversation), but we also have a shared onboarding system prompt that ~15% of users use verbatim (so some cross-session reuse exists).
3) Streaming: streaming is used for both short and long responses; for long responses streaming accounts for ~80% of those flows.
4) Tokenization: CSV counts include system prompt + user prompt; sample prompts in the CSV are labeled short/med/long.
5) Concurrency window: attached a 1-hour peak sample per-minute (see brightstack_traffic_declaration_v1.csv, column 'concurrent_sessions_20281103_1200-1300').
6) Quantization: product is comfortable with 8-bit quantization for 33B in production; we prefer to reserve FP16 for sensitive billing reconciliation flows only.
7) Compliance: US-only region required for production data; we need keys managed by our KMS.

We also attached a slightly cleaned CSV with the per-minute window and marked prompts. We’re aiming to finalize procurement ask by Nov 27 but are open to a sizing workshop this week if that helps.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachment: brightstack_traffic_declaration_v1.csv (time-series + prompt samples)

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightstack.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-15T15:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightStack traffic declaration — preliminary sizing review

Elena / team — thanks for the prompt follow-up and the sample window. Based on the declared traffic, model mix, and caching behavior, here is a conservative preliminary sizing to start procurement conversations. This is a pre-sales estimate (assumptions listed below) — we’ll refine after a short workload-stress workshop and a 24–48 hour PoC run.

Preliminary recommendation (baseline + peak capacity):
- Dedicated pool (baseline reserved): 12 x NVIDIA A100 80GB (sustained baseline capacity)
- Autoscale burst capacity: add 4 additional A100s on demand (scale to 16) for 10m peak windows (to handle burst up to ~1,200 RPS)
- Hot-path allocation: reserve 6 GPUs as 'hot' for KV-cached, low-latency serving (short flows), the remaining GPUs handle cold starts and long-response generation
- Model placement: 33B quantized to 8-bit on the hot GPUs; 13B on the cold pool for cost-effective handling; keep 2 GPUs with FP16 available for reconciliation/sensitive jobs
- Expected throughput (assumptions): baseline sustained ~120 RPS across pool, burst capacity to 1,200 RPS when autoscaled; target 95th latency ~200–350 ms for short flows when hot cache is effective
- Storage/Networking notes: recommend colocating pool in US-West region with ephemeral NVMe for KV caches and 25 Gbps networking per node

Estimated monthly reserved cost (ballpark): based on current Redwood Dedicated pricing and expected utilization, plan for a reserved commit that maps to 12 A100s (monthly commit) with burst credits to 4 extra GPUs. We will produce a formal cost estimate once you confirm region and commitment term (1yr vs 3yr).

Key assumptions & next steps:
- Assumes 70% intra-session cache reuse — if cross-session reuse is higher we can reduce GPUs on baseline by ~10–20%
- Assumes 8-bit quantization for 33B; if FP16 required for 33B the GPU / memory footprint increases and baseline GPUs needed will go up by ~25%
- We will run a 24–48h PoC with a small subset of representative traffic (you provide sample prompts and a replay window) to verify utilization and adjust autoscale policies.
- Marissa to schedule a 90-minute sizing workshop this week with BrightStack infra/product and our infra team (Vivek) — proposed slots: Thu 11/16 10:00–11:30 or Fri 11/17 13:00–14:30 PT. Please confirm preferred time.

Attachments: sizing_assumptions_BSK-v1.pdf (prelim assumptions + utilization model)

If this looks reasonable I’ll convert these assumptions into a formal dedicated offering and a draft term sheet for your procurement team.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Notes: attachments referenced above are included in the thread (brightstack_traffic_declaration_v1.csv, sizing_assumptions_BSK-v1.pdf).
